title: Fit UMich 2021 treadmill channels to a right-hand-rule sagittal convention and census ankle branch episodes
summary: Proposed a LocoHub sagittal frame (x walking direction, y up, z = person's right side out of the page, counterclockwise positive) and derived each signal's sign. Pure right-hand rule conflicts with clinical names in three places: pelvis anterior tilt, knee flexion angle and knee flexion moment (all negative under pure RHR). Every UM21 angle and moment channel was fitted (component x sign x offset) against independent evidence on 8 recordings, 16 legs (seed 20261030: AB07/i5, AB03/i5, AB08/d10, AB05/d5; disjoint seed 20261031: AB05/d10, AB04/d5, AB06/d5, AB01/i5). Best transform is component 1 with the published sign under the clinical convention for pelvis, hip, knee and ankle angles (best of 6 candidates in 16/16 legs each; median absolute residual against marker angles 0.03-0.14 deg pelvis, 0.65-2.6 hip, 0.97-3.3 knee, 0.41-1.5 ankle; opposite sign 1.8-31 deg). Under pure RHR the same component wins with sign -1 for pelvis and knee. Knee and ankle moments: component 1 wins against force-plate lever-arm moments in 15/16 and 14/16 legs; the published sign beats the flipped sign in 16/16 for both (knee needs x -1 under pure RHR); slope 0.75-0.91, so N*m/kg as stored. Hip moment is weak (component 1 wins in 8/16; published sign better in 14/16). New finding: power is stored in two layouts. In 42 recordings, components 1-3 are filled and component 1 = -(moment x joint speed). In 8 recordings (AB03/i10, AB04/d10, AB04/d5, AB04/i5, AB05/d10, AB05/d5, AB05/i0, AB05/i10), components 1-2 are zero and component 3 = +(moment x joint speed). Both layouts agree with force-plate moment x marker joint speed after that transform (power is invariant to the convention choice). Ankle: the AB07/i10 right run (1-based frames 11704-17134, 5429 frames, 34 strides) is the alternate Cardan solution (c1+180, 180-c2, c3+180) of a continuous ankle orientation. After re-expression, inside p1-p99 is [-16.6, 27.0], [1.1, 6.1], [-24.2, -3.4] deg vs outside [-15.9, 27.8], [0.5, 6.3], [-24.9, -0.5], and the frame-to-frame orientation step inside the run is 0.51 deg median, 2.43 deg at the 95th percentile (outside 0.64 and 2.77). The matrix identity (raw and re-expressed triples give the same rotation, 1.3e-15) holds for any triple; it checks the rule, it is not evidence. The run is not all clean: 13 frames change orientation by 20-171 deg in one frame (1-based clusters 11704-11713, 12704-12705, 14931-14932, 14973, 14986-14991). These are not alternate solutions; 29 of 31 inside strides are free of them. Census of all 500 joint-angle channels: alternate-branch frames in 3 ankle channels only (the AB07/i10 R episode plus AB05/d10 L 5 frames and AB06/d5 R 8 frames, which are glitches, not branch switches) and 21 FootProgress channels (left source-only). Also found: exact (0,0,0) fill in 241 of 500 angle channels, 23,386 frames between first and last heel strike in 87 channels.

(2) Midpoint CoP registration was too crude: a 3 cm change flipped component winners. The fitted shifts are 0.6-6.2 cm forward and -2 to +6 cm up, except one implausible leg (AB06/d5 R, -21 cm up, 1208 zero-fill frames). The midpoint result is kept as midpoint_registration_check. (3) Exact (0,0,0) triples are treated as missing.

The plate tilt used is the README slope, with sign from the marker path. The residual mean horizontal force is within 0.3 % body weight in 7 of 8 recordings; AB01/i5 shows -8.4 %, where the marker path gives 10 deg against the nominal 5 deg (unexplained, recorded).

decisions.question: Which sagittal sign rule should LocoHub adopt, with the person facing right and counterclockwise positive?
decisions.why: Segment angles have no anatomical name, so counterclockwise is the natural rule and composes cleanly (thigh = pelvis + hip). Joint columns are named flexion and dorsiflexion, and a knee flexion column that is negative in flexion invites misuse. A is cheapest and matches the UMich source exactly; C is the purest but contradicts the column names. Cross-dataset cost of B is unchecked.

options.label: Clinical names everywhere (pelvis forward tilt, knee flexion and knee flexion moment positive)
options.consequence: No sign changes for UMich 2021; the reference must stop calling it a right-hand rule for pelvis and knee. Reversible.

options.label: Segment angles counterclockwise, joint angles and moments positive in their named direction
options.consequence: Pelvis tilt flips sign (forward tilt negative) in every dataset that has it; joint columns unchanged. Reversible before release.

options.label: Counterclockwise for everything
options.consequence: Pelvis tilt, knee angle and knee moment flip in every dataset; knee flexion becomes negative under a flexion name. Reversible before release; outward-facing once released.

decisions.options_order: By how many signals differ from the published UMich sign: 0, 1, 3.
decisions.check: review_sheets/D-UM21-C03-1/index.html: the sign table shows exactly three red cells for C and one for B.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Moment and segment-angle columns cannot become standard in any dataset (C01 Q7); the treadmill pilot can still run with source copies.

decisions.question: How should the broken right-ankle stretch in the UMich 2021 incline-10 recording of one participant be released?
decisions.why: Inside the stretch, re-expressed values span the same 1st-99th percentile ranges as the leg's outside strides in all three components, and orientation changes by 2.4 degrees per frame at the 95th percentile (outside: 2.8). The 2 strides with sudden jumps stay out. B is the conservative fallback.
